{
  "IP": "neorv32_debug_dm",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Debug authentication validity",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Information": "The authentication result determines whether debug accesses and hart-control outputs are enabled, and its status is reported to the debug client. The result depends on the authenticator exchange.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "yes"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The authentication result is security-sensitive and is exposed in dmi_rsp_o.data(7) at line 549; the another-IP authenticator can change it from the exchange data at lines 740-745 under the black-box rule, altering access gates at lines 212-213 and control outputs at lines 500 and 505; an invalid result blocks authenticated reads and writes at lines 212-213; an injected or incorrectly accepted authentication exchange can enable debug control and halt behavior during normal operation through lines 740-745 and 500.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could exploit the authentication exchange or authenticator result to observe authentication status, obtain an unauthorized valid result, or keep the module unauthenticated and unavailable.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "dmi_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "dmi_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        740
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        745,
        754
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        549
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Selected hart identity",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Information": "The selected-hart setting identifies which hart receives debug control and which hart status is observed. Debug command execution and halt, resume, and reset-related operations depend on this selection.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "A debug write changes the selected-hart register at line 429, and the selection controls hart decoding and command routing at lines 487 and 298; an altered selection can direct a command to the wrong hart or leave the intended hart uncontrolled through lines 298, 366, 377, 384, and 500.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could modify the selected-hart value so halt or debug commands affect a different hart or fail to reach the intended hart.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "dmi_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "dmi_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        429
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        429
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        562
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Hart debug data exchange word",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Information": "The data word held in the debug data register is exchanged between the debug interface and the hart-side bus. Debug data transfers depend on this word being retained, written, and returned correctly.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The exchanged word can contain sensitive hart data and is returned through dmi_rsp_o.data and bus_rsp_o.data at lines 605 and 696; DMI and bus writes can modify it at lines 666 and 668; busy and access checks can reject or flag data-register transfers at lines 438, 464, and 626-628, withholding the exchange.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could read the returned data word, overwrite it with unauthorized data, or block the data-register transfer while a debug operation is busy.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "dmi_req_i.data",
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "dmi_rsp_o.data",
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        666,
        668
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        654,
        666,
        668
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        605,
        696
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Debug command busy state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Information": "The busy state indicates that a multi-step debug command is in progress and prevents conflicting debug-register accesses until the operation completes. Its status is returned to the debug client.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The busy flag is produced from the command state at line 339 and is reported at line 587; command and register writes are gated by it at lines 438, 443, 464, 469, and 474, so a manipulated or indefinitely asserted busy state can corrupt access sequencing or prevent further debug operations.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could cause the command state to remain busy, preventing new commands and data transfers or causing accesses to be rejected.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "dmi_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        339
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        587
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C5",
      "Concept Name": "Hart halt request",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Information": "The halt request is a control signal sent to the selected hart to stop its operation for debugging. Normal hart execution depends on this request not being asserted or suppressed without authorization.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "yes"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "A DMI control write supplies the halt control value at line 426 and the unit produces the selected, authenticated halt request at line 500; unauthorized assertion can stop hart execution and suppression can prevent a required debug halt through the same output gating at line 500; a debug or authentication bypass behavior can therefore stop normal hart operation through lines 500 and 212.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could inject or suppress the halt control so an unintended hart stops executing or a required halt request never reaches the hart.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "dmi_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "halt_req_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        426
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        500
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        500
      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Non-spared debug-register contents",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The activation, halt/resume/reset controls, hart status, command, command error, automatic-execution settings, and program-buffer words are debug-module register contents that only hold or decide what debug ports deliver, so the debug-module rule bars them as pieces of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Authentication exchange data and state other than validity",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "Authentication exchange words and authenticator state other than the valid flag are explicitly barred by the debug-module rule from becoming concepts of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Debug controller sequencing state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The controller state and its sequencing flags only order and gate debug operations, and the debug-module rule together with the sequencing-state rule bars them as independent information."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Debug reset request",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The reset control bit and ndmrstn_o only combine and drive a reset chain, so the clocks-and-resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "DMI and bus access commands",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The request addresses, directions, strobes, byte enables, and response handshakes are access-command or forwarded-transaction information rather than independent assets of this unit."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Fixed debug instruction ROM contents",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_dm",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The code ROM is a fixed constant at lines 149-182, and the RTL shows no attacker-modifiable sensitive state or required availability objective for its returned contents."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The authentication result determines whether debug accesses and hart-control outputs are enabled, and its status is reported to the debug client. The result depends on the authenticator exchange.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The authentication result is security-sensitive and is exposed in dmi_rsp_o.data(7) at line 549; the another-IP authenticator can change it from the exchange data at lines 740-745 under the black-box rule, altering access gates at lines 212-213 and control outputs at lines 500 and 505; an invalid result blocks authenticated reads and writes at lines 212-213; an injected or incorrectly accepted authentication exchange can enable debug control and halt behavior during normal operation through lines 740-745 and 500.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could exploit the authentication exchange or authenticator result to observe authentication status, obtain an unauthorized valid result, or keep the module unauthenticated and unavailable.

conceptual assets.information: The selected-hart setting identifies which hart receives debug control and which hart status is observed. Debug command execution and halt, resume, and reset-related operations depend on this selection.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A debug write changes the selected-hart register at line 429, and the selection controls hart decoding and command routing at lines 487 and 298; an altered selection can direct a command to the wrong hart or leave the intended hart uncontrolled through lines 298, 366, 377, 384, and 500.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could modify the selected-hart value so halt or debug commands affect a different hart or fail to reach the intended hart.

conceptual assets.information: The data word held in the debug data register is exchanged between the debug interface and the hart-side bus. Debug data transfers depend on this word being retained, written, and returned correctly.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The exchanged word can contain sensitive hart data and is returned through dmi_rsp_o.data and bus_rsp_o.data at lines 605 and 696; DMI and bus writes can modify it at lines 666 and 668; busy and access checks can reject or flag data-register transfers at lines 438, 464, and 626-628, withholding the exchange.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read the returned data word, overwrite it with unauthorized data, or block the data-register transfer while a debug operation is busy.

conceptual assets.information: The busy state indicates that a multi-step debug command is in progress and prevents conflicting debug-register accesses until the operation completes. Its status is returned to the debug client.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The busy flag is produced from the command state at line 339 and is reported at line 587; command and register writes are gated by it at lines 438, 443, 464, 469, and 474, so a manipulated or indefinitely asserted busy state can corrupt access sequencing or prevent further debug operations.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the command state to remain busy, preventing new commands and data transfers or causing accesses to be rejected.

conceptual assets.information: The halt request is a control signal sent to the selected hart to stop its operation for debugging. Normal hart execution depends on this request not being asserted or suppressed without authorization.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A DMI control write supplies the halt control value at line 426 and the unit produces the selected, authenticated halt request at line 500; unauthorized assertion can stop hart execution and suppression can prevent a required debug halt through the same output gating at line 500; a debug or authentication bypass behavior can therefore stop normal hart operation through lines 500 and 212.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject or suppress the halt control so an unintended hart stops executing or a required halt request never reaches the hart.

considered, not kept.reason: The activation, halt/resume/reset controls, hart status, command, command error, automatic-execution settings, and program-buffer words are debug-module register contents that only hold or decide what debug ports deliver, so the debug-module rule bars them as pieces of their own.

considered, not kept.reason: Authentication exchange words and authenticator state other than the valid flag are explicitly barred by the debug-module rule from becoming concepts of their own.
The controller state and its sequencing flags only order and gate debug operations, and the debug-module rule together with the sequencing-state rule bars them as independent information.
The reset control bit and ndmrstn_o only combine and drive a reset chain, so the clocks-and-resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
The request addresses, directions, strobes, byte enables, and response handshakes are access-command or forwarded-transaction information rather than independent assets of this unit.
The code ROM is a fixed constant at lines 149-182, and the RTL shows no attacker-modifiable sensitive state or required availability objective for its returned contents.
